extracted.intended_audience: corporate counsel, SEC reporting officers, and public company compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Practical legal guidance on when and what to disclose on Form 8-K for corporate events (changes in directors/officers, amendments to charter/bylaws, compensation events, blackouts, code of ethics waivers, shareholder votes and nominations, Reg FD disclosures, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Departure of principal officers or named executive officers (required facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: For departure of principal officers or named executive officers, or departure of directors not covered by Item 5.02(a): fact that the event occurred; date of event; effective date of event (SEC CDI Question 117.01). In the case of a refusal to stand for re-election, date of election in question (SEC CDI Question 117.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The company must provide the director with a copy of disclosures no later than the day the company files with the SEC, allow the director to furnish a letter stating agreement or disagreement with the disclosures, and file any director letter as an exhibit by amendment to the previously filed Form 8-K within two business days after receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of principal officer (required facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: For appointment of a principal officer: officer’s name and position; date of appointment; biographical information as required by Item 401(b) of Regulation S-K; family relationships required by Item 401(d); business experience required by Item 401(e); information regarding related person transactions required by Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a brief description of (i) any material plan, contract or arrangement (written or unwritten) to which the covered officer is a party or participates that is entered into or materially amended in connection with appointment and (ii) any grant or award to the officer or modification thereto under any such plan; if unavailable at initial filing, state that and file an amendment within four business days after information is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of directors (required facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: For election of directors: new director’s name; date of election; brief description of any arrangement or understanding under which the new director was selected; any board committees to which the new director has been or is expected to be named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If committee or related-person information is not determined at initial filing, include a statement to that effect and file an amendment within four business days after the information is determined. Include information regarding related person transactions as required by Item 404(a) and a brief description of any material plan, contract or arrangement (written or unwritten) entered into or materially amended in connection with the election and any grants/awards or modifications thereto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption or amendment of material compensatory plan (required facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: For adoption or amendment of material compensatory plan, contract, arrangement or award: a brief description of the terms and conditions of the plan, contract or arrangement and the amounts payable to the officer thereunder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items 5.02(c),(d),(e) require brief descriptions of both written and unwritten material plans, contracts or arrangements; the brief description need not comply with the more detailed Item 402 disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Later executive compensation determinations (required facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: For later executive compensation determinations: the name of the named executive officer; the salary and bonus information that was omitted from the Summary Compensation Table; a new total compensation figure for the named executive officer recalculated using the new salary and bonus information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the named executive officer is the principal executive officer and pay ratio disclosure under Regulation S‑K Item 402(u) is required, include the required pay ratio disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — unavailable information: statement + amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If certain information required by Items 5.02(c) and (d) is not determined or is unavailable at the time of the required Form 8-K filing, a company must include a statement to this effect in the filing and then must file an amendment to the Form 8-K containing the information within four business days after the information is determined or becomes available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule applies repeatedly across Items 5.02(c)-(d) and similar items; use the four-business-day amendment window when initial filing lacked specific details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — trigger: notice of decision to resign/retire/refuse re-election
rubrics_metrics.description: The obligation to report under Item 5.02(b) (other than corporate governance policy situations) is triggered by notice of a decision to resign, retire or refuse to stand for re-election provided by a director, principal officer or named executive officer whether or not the notice is written and without regard to whether the resignation/retirement/refusal is conditional or subject to acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussions or considerations regarding possible resignation, retirement or refusal to stand for re-election are not reportable. Companies must have disclosure controls/procedures to determine when a reportable notice has been communicated (SEC CDI Question 117.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — governance-policy resignation tender
rubrics_metrics.description: If a company has a corporate governance policy that requires a director to tender his or her resignation upon occurrence of an event (e.g., mandatory retirement age, job change, failing majority vote), the company must file a Form 8-K under Item 5.02(b) within four business days of the board’s decision to accept the director’s tender of resignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the board does not accept the tender (director remains on board), consider informing shareholders about governance policy enforcement (SEC CDI Question 117.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — termination notice timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the company must notify a named executive officer of the termination of employment a specified number of days prior to the date on which employment would end, an Item 5.02(b) Form 8-K filing requirement is triggered on the date the company notifies the officer of his or her termination, not on the effective date of termination (SEC CDI Question 217.05).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful tracking of the notice date is necessary to determine the filing deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — Summary Compensation Table exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure on Form 8-K is not triggered just because the named executive is no longer required to be included in the Summary Compensation Table as a result of the executive officer’s level of total compensation (SEC CDI Question 117.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate Summary Compensation Table inclusion thresholds with Form 8-K reporting triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — board decision not to nominate
rubrics_metrics.description: The board’s decision not to nominate a director for re-election when his or her term expires does not trigger a Form 8-K under Item 5.02; however, a Form 8-K would be required if, in response, the affected director resigns (SEC CDI Question 117.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision not to renominate alone is not a reportable resignation/termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — refusal to stand for re-election
rubrics_metrics.description: A director’s notice to the company that he or she refuses to stand for re-election requires a Form 8-K under this item, whether or not that notice is in response to an offer by the company to re-nominate the director (SEC CDI Question 117.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely file under Item 5.02(b) upon receipt of such notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — contingent resignation tied to shareholder sale
rubrics_metrics.description: When a director designated by a company’s majority shareholder gives notice that he or she will resign if the majority shareholder sells its entire holdings of company stock, this notice triggers an obligation to file an Item 5.02(b) Form 8-K, which should state clearly the nature of the contingency and the extent to which the resigning director can control the occurrence (SEC CDI Question 217.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose nature of contingency and degree of control the director has over the triggering event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — evaluate 5.02(a) vs 5.02(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a director resigns or refuses to stand for re-election, the company must carefully consider whether the event is reportable under Item 5.02(a) (matters related to operations/policies/practices) or Item 5.02(b) (termination/resignation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEC enforcement example: HP was found to have reported under 5.02(b) when disclosure under 5.02(a) was appropriate because the disagreement related to matters ‘related to the registrant’s operations, policies or practices.’ (Matter of Hewlett‑Packard Company, Release 34‑55801.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — termination includes reassignment/removal of duties
rubrics_metrics.description: A Form 8-K under Item 5.02(b) reporting the 'termination' of a principal officer or named executive officer is required where the officer has his or her duties and responsibilities removed or reassigned to others, even if the person remains employed or the person’s title remains the same (SEC CDI Question 117.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive functional change (loss of duties) can be a triggering 'termination' requiring Form 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — temporary turnover of duties
rubrics_metrics.description: When a principal officer temporarily turns duties over to another person, file a Form 8-K under Item 5.02(b) to report that the original officer has temporarily stepped down and under Item 5.02(c) to report that the replacement has been appointed; if the original returns, file to report the departure of the temporary officer and the re-appointment of the original (SEC CDI Question 217.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary surrender of duties triggers reporting when it is a turning over of power (extended leave or reassignment akin to leaving and being replaced), but routine vacations generally should not trigger Form 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — death of officer/director not triggering 5.02(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The death of a director or executive officer is not a triggering event under Item 5.02(b) of Form 8-K (SEC CDI Question 217.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No Item 5.02(b) filing required for death; consider other disclosure obligations where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — delay of 5.02(c) when public announcement planned
rubrics_metrics.description: If the company appoints a new principal officer and intends to make a public announcement by press release (or other means), the instructions to Item 5.02(c) permit delaying the due date of the Item 5.02(c) Form 8‑K until the day the other public announcement is made (SEC CDI Question 117.05).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, retirement/resignation/termination of the old principal officer triggers Item 5.02(b) immediately and cannot be delayed; no relief for related Form 3 filing under Section 16 (10 days) exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — director’s election date triggers 5.02(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of the director’s election to the board triggers the reporting requirement under Item 5.02(d), even if the director’s term will begin later. The Form 8-K should disclose the date on which the director’s term begins (SEC CDI Question 117.07).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose both election date and the date the term commences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice rule — committee reassignment exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a director’s appointment to the board and committee assignment were disclosed under Item 5.02(d) and the director is later assigned to a different committee, no new Form 8‑K or amendment is required provided the change in committee assignment was not contemplated at the time of the director’s initial election/appointment (Instruction 2 to Item 5.02 / SEC CDI Question 217.07).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, if initially not assigned to a committee and later assigned where change was not planned, no reporting required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality scope for plans/contracts and grants under Items 5.02(c)-(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike Item 5.02(e), which is limited to material compensatory arrangements, Items 5.02(c) and (d) require disclosure of any material plan, contract or arrangement entered into or materially amended in connection with the appointment, and any grant or award (regardless of the company’s assessment of materiality) made to a principal officer or director, or modified, under any such plan, contract or arrangement in connection with the appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies must evaluate materiality for each item; grants/awards made in connection with appointment must be disclosed even if the company views them as not material in other contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip — brief description of written and unwritten plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Items 5.02(c), (d) and (e) require a brief description of both written and unwritten material plans, contracts or arrangements with the covered executive officer or director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief description does not need to meet Item 402’s more detailed standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip — materiality determination and Exhibit filing
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of Items 5.02(c), (d) and (e), the company must determine what constitutes a material plan, contract or agreement for Item 5.02; some items covered by Item 601(b)(10)(iii) of Regulation S-K may be omitted from Item 5.02 reporting but must still be filed as an exhibit to the next Form 10‑Q or Form 10‑K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies remain obligated to file any plan/contract falling under Item 601(b)(10)(iii) as an exhibit to the next periodic report even if not material for Item 5.02 purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip — Item 5.02(e) scope (compensatory arrangements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure under Item 5.02(e) is required whether or not the specified event is in connection with other events triggering Items 5.02(a)-(d) or (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Item 5.02(e) reporting obligations independently when compensatory arrangements are adopted or materially amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip — equity award grants consistent with prior disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants or awards (or modifications) made pursuant to a plan, contract or arrangement that are materially consistent with previously disclosed terms need not be disclosed under Item 5.02(e), provided the grant/award/modification is disclosed when Item 402 requires (generally the next proxy statement) (Instruction 2 to 8‑K Item 5.02(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms of various equity award agreements are generally still required under the exhibit rules; companies should have on file forms that indicate term, termination provisions (post‑termination exercisability/vesting), change‑in‑control provisions, and material forfeiture/repurchase provisions; review vesting provisions for alignment with granting practices and alternatives used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip — cash bonus plan targets
rubrics_metrics.description: In the context of a material cash bonus plan, if prior Form 8‑K disclosure indicates the potential performance criteria upon which awards may be based, there is no need to file a Form 8‑K when the actual targets are set (SEC CDI Question 117.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the material payout is materially consistent with previously disclosed terms, no Form 8‑K is required; however, exercising discretion to pay the bonus despite unmet criteria does trigger Form 8‑K (SEC CDI Question 117.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip — confidentiality/competitive harm exception for targets
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting an annual non‑equity incentive plan award, the company is not required to disclose target levels for specific quantitative or qualitative performance factors or factors involving confidential trade secrets or commercial/business information the disclosure of which would cause competitive harm (SEC CDI Question 117.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standards in Instruction 3 to Regulation S‑K Item 402(b) and Instruction 2 to Item 402(e)(1) when omitting specific performance targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip — timing for board adoption vs shareholder approval
rubrics_metrics.description: When a company’s board adopts a new compensatory plan subject to stockholder approval, the obligation to file an Item 5.02(e) Form 8‑K is triggered on the date of stockholder approval of the plan, not on the date of board action (SEC CDI Questions 117.08 and 117.09).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor shareholder approval dates to determine filing triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip — employee-wide nondiscriminatory plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans, contracts and arrangements that do not discriminate in favor of executive officers and directors and that are generally available to all salaried employees (e.g., Section 423-qualified employee stock purchase plans) typically do not need to be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether plan scope/terms operate to favor executives before deciding on Item 5.02 reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip — internal procedures for Item 5.02(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: A company’s internal procedures need to be adequate to ensure that information required by Item 5.02(f) is known to those responsible for Form 8‑K filings; Item 5.02(f) often involves afterthought items such as payroll calculations and may be difficult to handle without strong internal controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear processes to identify triggering payments/grants/decisions and to determine precise triggering dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.03 — Amendments to Articles/Bylaws; Change in Fiscal Year (triggers)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8‑K is required if: (i) the company amends its charter or bylaws and the proposed amendment was not disclosed in a previously filed proxy or information statement; or (ii) the company determines to change the fiscal year used in its most recent filing by means other than shareholder submission or charter/bylaw amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This item only applies to companies with a class of equity securities registered under Section 12 of the Exchange Act. For reverse acquisition accounted acquisitions, disclose any intended change in fiscal year under Item 5.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.03 — Required disclosure details
rubrics_metrics.description: For amendments: effective date of amendment; description of the provision adopted or changed; description of previous provision, if applicable. For changes in fiscal year: date of such determination; date of the new fiscal year-end; form on which the report covering the transition period will be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A company is required to file only the text of the amended provision with the Form 8‑K but must file the complete document, as amended, with its next Form 10‑Q or Form 10‑K; may file full amended text redlined if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.04 — Temporary Suspension of Trading under Employee Benefit Plans (triggers)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8‑K is required if the company receives the notice required by Section 101(i)(2)(E) of ERISA relating to a temporary suspension of trading under an employer benefit plan, or, if such notice is not received by the company, the company transmits a timely notice to an affected officer or director within the time prescribed by Regulation BTR; or if the company transmits a timely updated notice as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common practice is to file the actual notice given to officers/directors as an exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.04 — Required disclosure details
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than the fourth business day after receipt/transmission: the reason(s) for the blackout period; description of plan transactions to be suspended or affected; description of the class of equity securities subject to the blackout; length of the blackout period by actual/expected beginning and ending dates or by calendar week description; the name/address/telephone of the person designated to respond to inquiries (or HR director if none).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When updated notice changes dates, include reasons for change and identify all material changes from prior notice. The notice to the SEC must describe how security holders can obtain actual beginning and ending dates during and for two years after the blackout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.04 — ERISA vs Regulation BTR distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: A Form 8‑K is not required to report notice of any blackout period that constitutes a blackout for ERISA notice requirements but does not constitute a 'blackout period' under Section 306(c) of the Sarbanes‑Oxley Act and Regulation BTR (SEC CDI Question 119.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether blackout meets Regulation BTR/Sarbanes‑Oxley definitions before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.05 — Amendments to Code of Ethics or Waiver (triggers)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8‑K is required if there is any amendment to a provision of the company’s code of ethics that applies to the principal executive officer, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer, controller or similar persons and that relates to any element of the code of ethics defined in Item 406(b) of Regulation S‑K; or if the company has granted a waiver (including implicit waiver) from such a provision to those officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Waiver' means approval of a material departure from a code provision; 'implicit waiver' means failure to take action within a reasonable time regarding a known material departure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.05 — Definition of 'Code of Ethics' elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Code of ethics means written standards reasonably designed to deter wrongdoing and to promote: honest and ethical conduct (including handling conflicts of interest); full, fair, accurate, timely and understandable disclosure in SEC reports and public communications; compliance with governmental laws/rules/regulations; prompt internal reporting of violations to an appropriate person; accountability for adherence to the code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an amendment or waiver touches any of these elements for covered officers, Item 5.05 disclosure is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.05 — Required disclosure and web‑posting alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Required disclosure: brief description of date and nature of any amendment; brief description of nature and date of waiver and person to whom a waiver was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The company need not file a Form 8‑K under this item if it posts the required information on its website within four business days and previously disclosed its internet address and intention to provide such disclosures by website in its most recent Form 10‑K. Website postings must remain posted for at least 12 months and retained for at least five years. Also review stock exchange rules (Nasdaq Rule 5610 and NYSE Section 303A.10) which may require disclosure within four business days and periodic disclosure for waivers extending beyond one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.07 — Submission of Matters to a Vote of Security Holders (triggers)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8‑K is required if a matter was submitted to a vote of security holders, through solicitation of proxies or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The triggering event occurs on the date the meeting ends and day one of the four-business-day filing period is the day after the meeting ends (SEC CDI Question 121A.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.07 — Required disclosure of shareholder vote results
rubrics_metrics.description: Required disclosure: date of the meeting and whether annual or special; a description of each election or other matter voted upon; number of votes cast for, against or withheld, number of abstentions and broker non‑votes for each matter, including separate tabulation for each nominee; for say‑on‑frequency votes, votes for each option and abstentions; description of terms of any settlement terminating a solicitation opposing director election/removal, including cost or anticipated cost; the company’s decision following a say‑on‑frequency vote as to future advisory vote frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final results aren't promptly available, disclose preliminary voting results and amend the Form 8‑K within four business days after final results are known. Disclosure of the company's frequency decision is due no later than 150 days after the meeting, but not later than 60 calendar days prior to the deadline for Rule 14a‑8 proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.07 — Filing mechanics and practical exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If no shareholder meeting was held, provide corresponding information about the submission of the matter to a vote. Instruction 3 allows a company that did not solicit proxies and previously filed board member names to simply state the board was re-elected in its entirety instead of restating each name and voting result. Instruction 5 allows certain wholly owned subsidiaries to omit this item in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A company may report Item 5.07 information in a periodic report filed on or before the date the Item 5.07 Form 8‑K would be due (General Instruction B.3). If a company reports annual meeting voting results in a Form 10‑Q or 10‑K and also intends to report its frequency decision in a Form 8‑K, the Form 8‑K must be filed as an amendment to the Item 5.07 Form 8‑K (8‑K/A) and not as a new Form 8‑K (SEC CDI Question 121A.04). Consider applicability of Item 5.02(e) if shareholders approved a compensatory plan at the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.08 — Shareholder Director Nominations (triggers)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8‑K is required if a company did not hold an annual meeting the previous year or the date of the annual meeting has been changed by more than 30 calendar days from the prior year and the company is required to include shareholder director nominees in its proxy materials pursuant to applicable state or foreign law or governing documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within four business days after the company determines the anticipated meeting date, the company must disclose the date by which a nominating shareholder or shareholder group must submit Schedule 14N required by Rule 14a‑18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.08 — Rule 14a‑18 / Schedule 14N timing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 14a‑18 provides that the deadline for submitting notice on Schedule 14N of shareholder nominees is either the date specified in the company’s advance notice bylaw or, if none, no later than 120 calendar days before the anniversary of the date the company mailed proxy materials for the prior year’s annual meeting, unless the company did not hold an annual meeting in the prior year or the meeting date changed by more than 30 days (in which case the nominating shareholder must submit notice a reasonable time before the company mails its proxy materials as specified by the company in an Item 5.08 Form 8‑K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 5.08’s four-business-day deadline appears in the last sentence of General Instruction B.1; assess company bylaws and procedural timelines when setting Schedule 14N deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 7.01 — Regulation FD Disclosure (use of Form 8‑K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 7.01 applies when the company wants to use Form 8‑K to satisfy its obligations under Regulation FD and desires the Form 8‑K to be deemed 'furnished' rather than 'filed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deadline under this item is determined by the requirements of Regulation FD; see filing mechanics on filing deadlines and the furnished vs filed distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 8.01 — Other Events (placeholder requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 8.01 covers disclosure of other events that a company considers material and appropriate to report on Form 8‑K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No expanded guidance in this chunk, but companies should use Item 8.01 when an event does not fit other specific items yet is material to investors.
